description: A free Chromium browser for the Mac: Arc's sidebar, Dia's polish. Chat on Discord: discord.gg/TdhuXrbcA6

latest_release.name: Ardia 0.2.46
latest_release.body:
## New

- **Onboarding is three steps.** Where you're coming from, how it looks, and a last few choices; everything else is set from the browser you picked, with Customize more… for the rest. It used to be eight steps and up to 24 screens. Helium is found on your Mac and imports from there, and Redo Setup… in Settings › General walks through it again from your current settings.
- **Auto Picture in Picture when you leave Ardia.** With Auto Picture in Picture on, a playing video pops out when Ardia's window goes out of sight and goes back into the page when you return. It works in WebKit tabs too.
- **Peek is on by default.** Links to other sites and links that open a new tab now open in a Peek, as in Arc. Settings you already changed stay as they are.
- **Clicking the address edits it in place.** The suggestions drop down from the field; ⌘T still opens the bar in the middle, and "In the centre" in Settings now applies to ⌘L only.
- **A tab switches when the mouse button goes down**, as in Chrome, Safari and Arc, which takes about a tenth of a second off every switch. Dragging, ⌘-click and ⇧-click work as before.
- **⌘W closes every selected tab**, and in a split it closes only the pane you're in. Close Split View in the pane's menu closes the whole split. Thanks, [@bwfront](https://github.com/ardia-browser/ardia/pull/1165).
- **⌥⌘← and ⌥⌘→ switch profiles**, as in Dia and Arc. Thanks, [@narasaka](https://github.com/mantrakp04/ardia/pull/1150).
- **⌥↩ in the command bar opens the address in Split View.** Thanks, [@bwfront](https://github.com/ardia-browser/ardia/pull/1142).
- **A "New tab opened" pill.** When a link opens in a background tab, a pill in the page's top right takes you to it. Thanks, [@luangjokaj](https://github.com/mantrakp04/ardia/pull/1203).
- **A collapsed group keeps the tabs you opened from it.** They stay under its header until you close them, as in Arc.
- **Pinch a Little Ardia window.** Spread to open it in the main window, pinch in to close it, as on a Peek.
- **A compact ⌘T, as a plugin.** Before you type, the command bar can skip your pinned tabs and Top Apps and list fewer open tabs. Install it from [ardia-plugins](https://github.com/mantrakp04/ardia-plugins); typing still finds every tab.
- **A borderless page frame**, and no frame in full screen when tabs are hidden. Thanks, [@bwfront](https://github.com/ardia-browser/ardia/pull/1181).
- **`ardia tabs --usage` shows what each tab costs.** Every tab's process, CPU and memory, hottest first, and `ardia tabs --pid` names the tabs behind a process `top` shows, so a tab draining the battery can be found from the terminal.
- **`ardia browse` gets an agent's job done in fewer steps.** An action answers with the text of whatever it opened, `read --scroll` reads a whole long list in one go, `fill` edits spreadsheet cells and picks from menus, and a drag lands where you aimed it.

## Faster

- **Switching tabs and opening a new one no longer slow down as tabs pile up.** Every row in the sidebar used to recheck itself on any change anywhere; now only the rows that changed do any work. With 200 tabs a switch does about a third of the bookkeeping it did.

## Fixed

- **Closing a window no longer closes tabs another window still shows.** With Share tabs across windows on, closing a window also closed the tabs of every profile the other window hadn't opened yet. They now move to the window you're still using, with their groups, splits and pages.
- **A profile keeps its extensions when the keychain key changes.** Every extension in the default profile could vanish at the next launch, with no message.
- **Watching upscaled video for a long time no longer crashes it.** After about 36 minutes at 30 fps, or 18 at 60, the video process could die.
- **Reopening a window you just closed keeps Back.** A window reopened in the seconds after closing came back with its tabs but none of their history. A window now closes at once, so ⇧⌘T brings back each tab with Back and Forward

detail.readme:
Touch grass.

Arc’s sidebar and Dia’s polish on real Chromium.
Free and open source. Ads and trackers stay out.

Download Ardia 0.2.46 for Mac

128 MB DMG · macOS 14 Sonoma or later · Apple Silicon · Notarized by Apple
Like your paint wet? The nightly has every fix the day it’s made, smudges and all.
Homebrew: brew install ardia-browser/tap/ardia
ardia.dev · What’s new · All releases · Discord

## Lose the toolbar. Move the address bar into the sidebar and the page runs all the way to the top of the window. ## Two pages, one window. Drag a tab onto the page. Up to three panes, side by side or stacked. ## Refuses to leave the picture. Switch tabs mid-video and it floats along in the corner. Go back to its tab and it slips back into the page. ## Your extensions come along. The Chrome Web Store just works, its button says Add to Ardia, and Sync takes them to your other Macs. ## Ads and trackers stay out. The full uBlock Origin is built in, cookie banners included. Google’s pings are compiled out. Crash reports are opt-in and never carry your sites or searches. ## Also in there - **Work stays at work.** Each profile keeps its own logins, history, extensions and colour. Swipe the sidebar to switch. - **Little Ardia.** ⌥⌘N opens a small window with one page and no sidebar. - **Groups on contact.** Drop a tab on a tab and they’re a group, named for you. - **Moves in for you.** Bookmarks, history, passwords and logins from Chrome, Safari, Firefox, Arc, Dia and five more. Arc’s spaces, pinned tabs and themes too. - **Paints like Arc.** Gradient themes per profile: up to three colours, some grain, some blur. - **Syncs through your iCloud.** End-to-end encrypted, in a folder in your own iCloud Drive. No server of ours in the middle. - **Command bar.** ⌘L finds tabs, history and bookmarks, does your sums, and knows doc.new and 16 friends. - **Tidies up.** ⌥⌘K sweeps the tabs you haven’t touched into Recently Cleaned. - **Clean links.** Copy a link and the tracking junk stays behind. - **Naps when you do.** Background tabs past your latest five freeze, and sleep after half an hour. - **Sits still.** Idles under half a percent of CPU with a tab open. - **Updates itself.** Quietly, then shows you what changed. ## It’s actually Chromium. Not WebKit. Not Electron. Every window is Chrome’s own, so sites, extensions and DevTools behave like they do in Chrome. | Part | Details | Status | | --- | --- | --- | | Engine | Chromium 157, on Chrome’s own framework. | ✓ Yes | | De-Googled | Google’s background services stripped out. | ✓ Yes | | H.264 and AAC | The codecs Chromium leaves out. | ✓ Yes | | DevTools | Docked, with device mode. Like Chrome. | ✓ Yes | | Sync | End-to-end encrypted, through your own iCloud Drive. | ✓ Yes | | Translate | On your Mac. Nothing leaves it. | ✓ macOS 26 | | Passkeys | Touch ID yes. iCloud Keychain waits on Apple. | ~ Partly | | Netflix and DRM | Streaming sites open in WebKit, where they play. Widevine in Chromium waits on Google. | ~ Partly | | Intel Macs | Apple Silicon only. | ✗ No |

Download Ardia 0.2.46

It’s 128 MB and one drag into Applications.
Not on a Mac? Watch › Custom › Releases up top and GitHub tells you when it is.

--- # Build it yourself A macOS browser that looks and feels like [Dia](https://diabrowser.com): Chrome's own framework from our patched Chromium with our layer on top (ArdiaCore), an Expo + React Native macOS shell, and Metal shaders reconstructed from Dia's own New Tab effects. ``` apps/ browser/ Expo + react-native-macos app (UI in src/, Xcode project in macos/) packages/ ardiacore/ The engine: Chromium 157's framework with our layer (Chrome tabs hosted in our views), JS API in src/ shell/ Native menu bar + shortcuts → JS, windows, SF Symbols, native primitives shaders/ Metal: New Tab effects + grained OKLab window backdrop import/ Import from other browsers (bookmarks, history, passwords, Arc spaces) core/ Pure TS: omnibox input → URL, suggestions, Dia-style breadcrumbs (tested) ``` ## Run it Requires Xcode 26+, CocoaPods, Node 24 (pinned in `.nvmrc`), pnpm 11. ```bash pnpm install ``` The engine (Chrome's framework, built from our patched Chromium) comes prebuilt: with no local engine build, the app's build downloads the one matching your checkout's `engine/` (about 110 MB, once; Apple Silicon only) and checks it against `packages/ardiacore/prebuilt-engines.tsv`. Every release whose engine changed publishes one. If `main`'s engine is newer than the last release's, work from a release tag (`v0.2.30`, say), or run `packages/ardiacore/scripts/fetch-engine.sh --nearest` to build against the newest prebuilt anyway. Passkeys and saved cards need our team ID and won't work in a build signed by anyone else. To change the engine itself (anything under `engine/`), build it from source: Chrome's framework from our patched Chromium tree in `~/chromium-build` (Chromium 157.0.8103.50 with the patch series in `engine/patches`; `docs/engine-build.md` › "Rebuilding", then `engine/chromium/apply.sh`, `engine/ardiacore/apply.sh` and `autoninja -C out/Release_GN_arm64 chrome_framework`; the first build takes about 2 hours). The app's build stages it from there when it exists. ```bash pnpm pods ``` In one terminal, start Metro: ```bash pnpm dev ``` In another, build and launch the Debug app (on its own data, `~/Library/Application Support/Ardia Dev`, or `ARDIA_DATA_DIR`): ```bash pnpm macos ``` Other tasks: `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm shaders:check` (compiles the embedded Metal offline), `scripts/agent/build-app --config Release` (a Release `.app` with a Hermes bytecode bundle in `apps/browser/build-`, under the shared build locks; `--help`). Signed releases (DMG, Sparkle zip and appcast) are built by the Release workflow with `scripts/release.sh`, see `docs/releasing.md`. Shortcuts: ⌘T new tab, ⌘L command bar, ⌘W close, ⇧⌘T reopen, ⌘S sidebar, ⌘[ / ⌘] back/forward, ⌘R reload, ⌘1–⌘9 select tab, ⌃Tab cycle. ## How Dia's New Tab light works Dia 1.50 turns this light off along with its rebrand (a painted mark, a single-colour power-up band and a halo around the bar; `docs/dia-spec.md` › "1.50 Sunglow"), and so does Ardia. The reconstruction left the tree with it: `git show f2c0e251:packages/shaders/ios/AreaLightView.swift`. These findings come from disassembling the Metal libraries in `Dia.app` (v1.49.1) with `xcrun metal-objdump`. `BoostBrowser_PowerUp.bundle/default.metallib` contains `breathingAreaLightFragment`, which the Swift class `NewTabPage.NewTabAreaLightView` hosts. The reconstruction was `AreaLightView.swift` (above). - **The command bar is a light source.** Dia models the bar as a rounded-rectangle area light floating `lift` points above the page. Each pixel receives the closed-form irradiance of that rectangle: the solid-angle formula, one `atan` term per corner, times 1/2π. Rounded corners subtract (1 − π/4) of each corner square. The result is a physically correct penumbra: a higher lift gives a softer, wider glow. - **Falloff** is reshaped from inverse-square to `(h/d)^falloff`, where `d` is the distance to the emitter's rounded-rect surface rather than to its centre. - **Colour** is Dia's brand spectrum (`ProgressBarColor2…7` in its asset catalog): blue `#0358F7`, steel `#5092C7`, lavender `#E1E1FE`, yellow `#FFD400`, orange `#FA3D1D` and magenta `#FD02F5`. It is laid out as a wrapping, slightly diagonal gradient that scrolls every 20 s. IQ's 2D simplex noise warps the gradient under the bar, and the warp fades out into the penumbra. - **Dark mode** treats the light as HDR emission and applies the Hable/Uncharted-2 filmic tonemap (white point 11.2), with alpha set to Rec.709 luminance. **Light mode** keeps the flat palette colour and uses the irradiance as opacity. - **Finishing:** alpha fades over the top 50 pt and bottom 200 pt of the view, and ±3/255 triangular dither (Dave Hoskins' `hash12`) prevents banding in the long soft falloff. - **Animation:** the shader itself only scrolls the colours. The lift-off intro and the slow "breathing" come from the CPU, which animates `lift` and `intensity`. Those curves live in Dia's Swift code, so the ones here (quartic ease-out over 1.1 s, ±7% intensity on a 5.5 s sine) are my approximation. The **window backdrop** comes from `ARC_WindowThemeUI.bundle` (`gradientFragment` + `renderFragment`). Gradient stops are stored and mixed in **OKLab**, then converted to linear sRGB and gamma-encoded in the shader. A tiled grain texture is then multiply-blended on top. `WindowBackdropView` does the same with procedural grain. Only math and colour values are reused. No Dia images, fonts or binaries are copied into this repo. ## Architecture notes - **Why Expo SDK 54:** `react-native-macos` tops out at 0.81, which pairs with Expo SDK 54 (whose `ExpoAppDelegate` / `ExpoReactNativeFactory` have macOS code paths). - **Legacy architecture.** react-native-macos 0.81's Fabric support is experimental, so the app runs on the legacy architecture. One consequence: Expo's legacy view-manager adapter instantiates a module's *first* view class for every view it declares, so each native view has its own module. - **Metro, not `expo start`.** Metro runs through the react-native-macos CLI. `metro.config.js` redirects `react-native` → `react-native-macos` for `platform=macos`, because defining our own `resolveRequest` replaces the redirect the CLI would install. - **No Reanimated.** It has no macOS build for 0.81; animations use RN's `Animated`. - **Monorepo paths.** pnpm is set to `nodeLinker: hoisted` because CocoaPods and Metro resolve `react-native-macos` by path. The Podfile rewrites `REACT_NATIVE_PATH` to the hoisted location and raises every pod's deployment target to 14.0, since Xcode 26+ rejects the 11.0 some Expo pods declare. - **Native subviews** are sized in `setFrameSize`, not `layout()`. RN macOS assigns frames directly and never autoresizes subviews. - **Shaders** are Metal source embedded in Swift and compiled at runtime (once per class, cached). This keeps the pods free of a metallib build phase. ## Status Feature parity with Dia (everything but its AI) is tracked row by row in [docs/dia-feature-parity.md](docs/dia-feature-parity.md); releases and their notes are at [ardia.dev/release-notes](https://ardia.dev/release-notes). ## License Ardia as distributed is licensed under the [GNU General Public License v3](LICENSE), because its engine is built with GPL-3.0 patches. Ardia's own source files are under the [Apache License 2.0](LICENSE.Apache-2.0). It builds on Chromium, carries a few of the Chromium Embedded Framework's patches to Chromium (BSD-3-Clause), and bundles uBlock Origin, each under its own license; see [NOTICE](NOTICE). Every release links its source.
